title: The Ambassador in the Sun: Daily Sunrise and Sunset as the Two Cosmic Mysteries
arc: The teaching reads the sun's daily rising and setting as a single revealed sign in which two great mysteries of the Ambassador are continually manifest: the First Man's primal shining upon the sons of Darkness at the cosmos's beginning, and the last Extraction at its consummation when all light is gathered home and Death is shut into the sunless night.
reading:
This chapter teaches that the sun overhead is not merely a luminary but a daily disclosure of the Third Ambassador's whole work. Its rising and its setting are two great mysteries, and the entire arc of redemption — from the first contest with the King of Darkness to the final consummation of the cosmos — is rehearsed visibly every day for those who can read correspondence.

The first mystery is the sunrise. When the sun shines forth, every creature of flesh draws itself out from the dark places where it has lain, and stands exposed against the Radiance. All men open their mouths, and the whole of humanity together with the creatures comes out onto the Cross of Light that "stands fast in stillness." The teaching tells us explicitly that this corresponds to the mystery of the First Man: at the very moment the divine attributes came forth from the Greatness, they shone upon all the sons of Darkness, and that hour the sons of Darkness were forced out of their storehouses, their powers, and their dwelling-places — they had to leave their caverns and the Deep of darkness, and the body of their Five Sons (the five forms of self-love mounted upon the receptive natural) was broken. Sunrise, then, is the standing image of the original descent of Divine Truth into the realm of the proprium: the moment when light entered the mingled state, drove falsity out of its hiding, and laid the basis for everything that creatures of the natural now do reflexively each morning when they emerge into the day. This, the chapter says, is the first contest.

The second mystery is the sunset. When evening comes, men and cattle alike go back into their hiding-places of darkness, the multitude of the cosmos shut their mouths, and the night of darkness comes upon them; they dwell within their night in their hidden places. The teaching reads this not as defeat but as a great Raising-up — for it images the consummation. At the end, the sun itself "shall be chosen forth out of the cosmos" together with the chosen ones; the elect go inward to their mansions and are hidden. This corresponds to the moment when the entire Light is purified and chosen out of the cosmos, when every thing is dissolved and the last Andrias gathers inward into the depiction of the fullness — the final statue of redeemed light ascending upward into the Light. The same evening movement, however, has its inverse for what is not light: the Enemy, Death himself, and the blasphemers who loved the Darkness go in with him to the place of judgment, into the souls of those bound to him, and are shut up in the sunless region of the night of darkness — the bolos, the final compacted clod where evil is fixed forever, until it is said of them only that "a Light shines for them" from outside, no longer within. Sunset is thus simultaneously the gathering of the elect homeward and the sealing of unredeemed darkness into its eternal night.

The spiritual argument is therefore that one and the same operation of the Ambassador works at both ends of the cosmic day: his rising drives falsity out of its concealments and exposes every creature to discrimination, and his setting carries refined light upward while binding what refused light into its own sunless place. What looks like an ordinary diurnal cycle is in fact the two-fold rhythm of redemption — descent and extraction, manifestation and consummation — visible "daily" in the one Illuminator who radiates. The reader is told to see the sun as the Ambassador's standing sign: every dawn rehearses the First Man's primal victory over the sons of Darkness, and every dusk rehearses the last Andrias's gathering of all light into the fullness while the Enemy is shut into his tomb.
